parrafos: A supermarket, grocery store (or just grocery) is a retail store that sells food. Most grocery stores sell fresh fruit, vegetables, seafood, meat, and other prepared foods.
The person who controls a grocery store is called a grocer. A grocer will order food from farmers or other people who send out farmers food to other grocery stores and restaurants.

There are a range of different types and sizes of grocery stores. Some grocery stores are small community stores with a limited range of items. Other grocery stores are large, with a wide selection of food items.
They may also sell household cleaning and laundry supplies, and hygiene items (soap, toothpaste, etc.). They may also contain a pharmacy (known as a drug store or chemist in some places).

Items at a grocery store can be sold in one of two ways. Most fruits, vegetables, meat, and seafood are usually sold by weight (for example, apples cost 99 cents per pound), while other items are usually sold by quantity (for example, table salt costs $1.59 for each box). Not all items are the same price at each grocery store. Also, every week, some items at grocery stores cost less that what it normally would cost (we say that these items are "on sale"), so people would want to go buy them since they don't have to pay as much as they would normally have to get that item. Many grocery stores print a flyer that shows which items are on sale that week. These flyers are then sent to other people in the mail, who would read the flyer and go to the store to buy the items shown in it.

Supermarkets are large grocery stores that sell a large variety of fresh and packaged food and other consumer or household products. Supermarkets are divided into sections, such as bakery, dairy, produce (fruits and vegetables), frozen, meat, and deli, along with a "general grocery" section where one can find packaged goods, cleaning supplies, and personal hygiene items. Many supermarkets today now also sell hot, prepared food that is ready to eat, or contains a food court with different fast food shops. The term "supermarket" usually refers to a larger store than the term "grocery store."

A hypermarket is a very large supermarket that is part of a larger general merchandise store such as Walmart, which also sells clothes, electronics, household hardware, and other items. It can be said to be a hybrid (or combination) of a grocery store and a department store. These stores are mainly found in suburbs where there is a lot of room to build and near where people live.

Until the 20th century, grocery stores were small. The owner, called a shopkeeper, would ask the customer what he or she would like to buy. The shopkeeper would then get the items, bring it to the customer, and put them in bags which the customer would take with them. He would then calculate how much the customer has to pay, and take the money from the customer. The customer then took the bags of items out of the store by him/herself.

Today, most groceries stores are too big for one person to take care of. Because of this, customers must find the items they wants by themselves. Most often, the customer takes a shopping basket or shopping cart and put the items into the basket or cart. For some items, like meat and seafood, the customer still has to have an employee get or prepare the item. When customers have finished selecting, they bring the items to the "checkout", where a person called a cashier scans the customer's items into a cash register (or a computer as part of a point of sale system) and then takes the customer's payment. Supermarkets typically accept payment by cash, debit cards, and/or credit cards. In the 21st century, there are so-called self-checkout systems where customers scan the items themselves.

Many large supermarkets also have a loyalty program, where a customer can earn points by purchasing products. When a customer has enough points, a discount or reward is given. These programs are meant to make customers come back to the same store again and again.

resumen_es: An informative text explaining what a grocery store is, the types of shop (neighbourhood stores, supermarkets and hypermarkets), how prices are set and reduced, and how shopping has changed since the 20th century.
nivel_motivo: The retail vocabulary (“retail”, “point of sale system”, “loyalty program”, “general merchandise”) and the average sentence length place it above A2.

ideas_clave.idea: A grocery store is a shop that retails food, run by a grocer who buys supplies from farmers or distributors.
Grocery stores range from small neighbourhood shops to large outlets that also stock cleaning, hygiene and even pharmacy products.
Goods are priced either by weight or per unit, prices differ between shops, and weekly discounts are advertised through printed leaflets.
Supermarkets are big stores organised into departments that may also offer ready-made meals or food courts.
Hypermarkets combine a supermarket with a department store and are usually located in the suburbs, where space is available.
Shopping has shifted from shopkeepers serving customers personally to self-service, with checkouts staffed by cashiers or operated by customers themselves.
Loyalty schemes reward repeat purchases with points that can be exchanged for discounts.

resumen_modelo: The text explains what a grocery store is: a retail business selling food, managed by a grocer who obtains supplies from farmers or intermediaries. Such shops vary in size, from small local stores with a limited range to large outlets that also offer household products, toiletries and sometimes a pharmacy. Prices are set either by weight or per item, they differ from one store to another, and weekly special offers are advertised through leaflets sent by post. Supermarkets, which are divided into departments and may even include food courts, are larger than ordinary grocery stores, while hypermarkets, typically found in the suburbs, combine a supermarket with a department store. Moreover, the way people shop has changed considerably: until the twentieth century the shopkeeper fetched and packed every item, whereas customers nowadays serve themselves and pay at a checkout, increasingly a self-service one. Finally, many chains run loyalty schemes designed to encourage customers to return.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: A grocer may buy food from farmers.
preguntas.cita: A grocer will order food from farmers
preguntas.explicacion: The text states that the grocer orders food from farmers or from middlemen who distribute it.

preguntas.pregunta: Apart from food, what may some grocery stores contain?
preguntas.cita: They may also contain a pharmacy (known as a drug store or chemist in some places).
preguntas.explicacion: Only the pharmacy is mentioned. Banks, post offices and petrol stations do not appear in the text.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 3 a word that, in some places, means a pharmacy.
preguntas.pregunta: Find a word used in some places for 'pharmacy'.
preguntas.cita: known as a drug store or chemist in some places
preguntas.explicacion: “Chemist” is the British term and “drug store” the American one; both mean a pharmacy (es: farmacia).

preguntas.pregunta: How are fruits and vegetables usually sold?
preguntas.cita: Most fruits, vegetables, meat, and seafood are usually sold by weight
preguntas.explicacion: Fruit, vegetables, meat and seafood are sold by weight. Selling by the unit applies to other products, such as salt; the text also says that prices are not the same in all shops.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Flyers showing weekly offers are only available inside the store.
preguntas.cita: These flyers are then sent to other people in the mail
preguntas.explicacion: The flyers are sent by post to potential customers; they are not handed out only inside the shop.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 4 an expression meaning “reduced in price, on offer” (es: rebajado, de oferta).
preguntas.pregunta: Find an expression meaning 'offered at a reduced price'.
preguntas.cita: we say that these items are "on sale"
preguntas.explicacion: “On sale” in American English means “on offer” or “reduced in price” (es: en oferta, rebajado). Careful: in British English “for sale” means “available to buy” (es: en venta).

preguntas.pregunta: Which section of a supermarket sells fruit and vegetables?
preguntas.explicacion: The “produce” section is fruit and vegetables. “Deli” is cold meats and ready-made food, “dairy” is milk products and “general grocery” refers to packaged goods.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Hypermarkets are mostly located in city centres.
preguntas.cita: These stores are mainly found in suburbs where there is a lot of room to build
preguntas.explicacion: The text places hypermarkets mainly on the outskirts, where there is space to build, not in the centre.

preguntas.pregunta: Describe the role of the shopkeeper in small grocery stores before the 20th century.
respuestas: The shopkeeper asked customers what they wanted, collected the items, packed them in bags, worked out the total price and took the payment; customers did not pick the goods themselves.
preguntas.cita: The owner, called a shopkeeper, would ask the customer what he or she would like to buy.
preguntas.explicacion: The answer should show that the grocer did the whole process, unlike today’s self-service.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Self-checkout systems have reduced the number of cashiers employed by supermarkets.
preguntas.explicacion: The text describes self-checkouts, but says nothing about their effect on cashiers’ jobs.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 8 a word for the person who takes the money at the checkout.
preguntas.pregunta: Find the word for the person who scans the items and takes payment.
preguntas.cita: a person called a cashier scans the customer's items into a cash register
preguntas.explicacion: A “cashier” is the person who takes payments (es: cajero, cajera); they work with the “cash register”.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the main purpose of loyalty programs?
opciones: To reduce the price of fresh food
To make customers return to the same store
To collect money for local charities
To replace payment by credit card
respuestas: To make customers return to the same store
preguntas.cita: These programs are meant to make customers come back to the same store again and again.
preguntas.explicacion: The stated aim is customer loyalty. Discounts are the means, not the end, and neither donations nor card payments have anything to do with these programmes.

preguntas.pregunta: What marketing tools do grocery stores use to attract customers, according to the text?
respuestas: They offer weekly discounts on some items, advertise them in flyers mailed to people's homes, and run loyalty programs that reward repeat purchases with points and discounts.
preguntas.cita: Many grocery stores print a flyer that shows which items are on sale that week.
preguntas.explicacion: This is a synthesis question: combine the weekly offers and the flyers (paragraph 4) with the loyalty programmes (paragraph 9).
